recognize_zh: 中倍 H&E 可見血管腔內充滿均質粉紅色的血栓（左側一條長形、中央一個圓形），周圍被許多卵圓至腎形核的上皮樣組織球包圍，下方另有兩顆大型多葉核的不典型細胞，符合 EBV 陽性黏膜皮膚潰瘍中常見的血管栓塞與組織球反應。
features: Small vessels with lumina occluded by homogeneous eosinophilic thrombus material
Surrounding plump epithelioid histiocytes with oval to reniform nuclei, fine chromatin and pale cytoplasm
Two large atypical cells with multilobated, hyperchromatic nuclei in the lower field
Scattered small lymphocytes and occasional apoptotic bodies
Fibrillary to edematous eosinophilic stroma at right
describe_en: Sections show small vessels whose lumina are occluded by homogeneous eosinophilic thrombi, surrounded and infiltrated by numerous epithelioid histiocytes with oval to kidney-shaped nuclei. Scattered small lymphocytes and apoptotic bodies are present, and two large atypical cells with multilobated hyperchromatic nuclei are seen in the lower field. Well-formed granulomas and organisms are not identified. Vascular thrombosis with perivascular histiocytic reaction and scattered atypical large cells is a recognized feature of EBV-positive mucocutaneous ulcer and should prompt EBER in situ hybridization.

ddx.vs: Shows true angiocentric infiltration of vessel walls by EBV+ large B cells with fibrinoid necrosis, usually in lung, rather than luminal thrombi within a circumscribed mucocutaneous ulcer.
Angiodestructive growth with coagulative necrosis by atypical medium-sized cells that are CD56+ and cytoplasmic CD3+, with EBER in the neoplastic T/NK cells rather than B cells.
Features necrotizing vasculitis with geographic basophilic necrosis, multinucleated giant cells and ANCA positivity, without EBER-positive atypical B cells.
